title: Lab: teach Qwen to solve maths word problems
summary: Run a complete GRPO project on a free Colab GPU: score Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on held-out GSM8K questions, train it with format and correctness rewards, read the curves and real answers, and save your first reasoning model.
learningObjectives: Run a full GRPO pipeline: baseline, smoke test, training, held-out evaluation, saving
Read TRL's training log on day one and judge noisy metrics by their trend
Compare before and after answers and tell genuine reasoning from format gaming
Write a short, honest lab report of a training run

studyGuide.mentalModel: A science experiment with a control group. Measure the untrained model first, change one thing (GRPO training), measure again on the same unseen questions, then read the actual answers to understand why the numbers moved.
keyIdeas: Always record a baseline on held-out questions before training; without it, the after number means nothing.
A 10-step smoke test catches crashes and memory errors before you commit an hour.
With 2 questions per step, metrics are noisy; read trends over 20 to 30 steps.
Our accuracy requires the number inside <answer> tags, so some improvement may come from format alone.
Save before the Colab session ends: merge the adapter and upload or download it.
misconceptions: A rising training reward does not guarantee higher held-out accuracy.
A filled <think> block is not proof of reasoning; read whether the steps lead to the answer.
A 0.5B model will not become strong at maths in 250 steps; modest gains are a normal outcome.
A LoRA adapter folder is not a standalone model; it needs the base model or merging.
recallPrompts: What are the two numbers the evaluation reports, and what does each measure?
Why run a smoke test before the full run?
Name three things to look for when reading a before/after answer.
What did DeepSeek-R1 find about RL versus distillation for small models?
studyGuide.explainBackPrompt: Explain to a friend how you would prove that your GRPO training actually made the model better at maths, rather than just better at pleasing the grader.

quiz.prompt: Why does the lab score the untrained model before training?
options: To warm up the GPU
Because TRL requires an evaluation before training
To have a control: without a before number, an after number cannot show improvement
To pick the best questions for training
quiz.explanation: The baseline on the same held-out questions is the control group. The improvement is after minus before.

quiz.prompt: Accuracy only counts an answer if its number is inside <answer> tags. What does this mean for interpreting a jump in accuracy after training?
options: Part of the jump may come from the model learning the format, not only from better maths
The jump must be entirely due to better arithmetic
The jump is impossible
It means the test set leaked into training
quiz.explanation: A model that solved problems but ignored the tags scored zero before. Learning the format alone can raise accuracy. Reading real answers helps separate the two.

quiz.prompt: Step 120 shows correctness reward 0.9, step 125 shows 0.1. What is the best reading?
options: The model forgot everything in 5 steps
The run crashed
Training should be stopped immediately
Normal noise: each step uses only 2 questions, so judge the trend over many steps
quiz.explanation: With 2 questions x 8 answers per step, one easy or hard question swings the number. The rolling average shows the real trend.

quiz.prompt: After training, many answers look like <think>Let me solve this.</think><answer>17</answer>. What should you conclude?
options: The model is reasoning perfectly
The format reward is being satisfied with almost no thinking; check accuracy and consider a stricter reward
The GPU ran out of memory
The evaluation is broken and should be ignored
quiz.explanation: The format reward accepts any non-empty think block. Filler thinking is a mild form of gaming; the correctness numbers and examples tell you whether maths improved.

quiz.prompt: What is the difference between the LoRA adapter folder and the merged model?
options: The adapter only works on top of the base model; the merged model contains base plus adapter and loads on its own
They are identical files with different names
The merged model is untrained
The adapter is bigger than the merged model
quiz.explanation: LoRA trains small extra matrices. Merging adds them into the base weights to make a standalone model that loads with plain transformers.
